translationRepairs: The inner attendant Chen Yuan had favor at the Deposed Sovereign's Palace and was given an additional appointment as deputy overall commander of western Zhejiang.
The inner attendant Chen Yuan had favor at Deshou Palace and was given an additional appointment as deputy overall commander of western Zhejiang.
德壽宮 names Gaozong's retirement palace Deshou; 'Deposed Sovereign's Palace' invents a false palace title.

When Guangzong took the throne, an urgent recall was issued before Ruyu arrived. Palace attendant Fan Chuyi charged him with tardiness. He was named prefect of Tanzhou, declined, and was given Taipingzhou instead.

When Guangzong took the throne, an urgent recall was issued before Ruyu arrived. Palace Censor Fan Chuyi charged him with tardiness. He was named prefect of Tanzhou, declined, and was given Taipingzhou instead.
殿中侍御史 is a Censorate remonstrance post (Palace Censor), not a palace attendant.

When Guangzong received the abdication, an urgent summons was sent but Ruyu had not yet arrived; Palace Attendant Fan Chuyi impeached him for delaying his orders; he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou, declined, and was changed to Taipingzhou.

When Guangzong received the abdication, an urgent summons was sent but Ruyu had not yet arrived; Palace Censor Fan Chuyi impeached him for delaying his orders; he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou, declined, and was changed to Taipingzhou.
Same office 殿中侍御史; literal 'Palace Attendant' is the same institutional error.
Ruyu also asked Prince Xiuxiu Bogui to help reconcile them, and feeling between the two courts was restored.
Ruyu also asked Bogui, the succeeding Prince of Xiu, to help reconcile them, and feeling between the two courts was restored.
嗣秀王伯圭 is Bogui as succeeding Prince of Xiu; 'Prince Xiuxiu' misreads 嗣秀 as a personal name.
Ruyu also entrusted the heir apparent's younger brother, Prince of Xiuxiu Bogui, to mediate and care for them, and thus feeling between the two palaces was opened.
Ruyu also entrusted the succeeding Prince of Xiu, Bogui, to mediate and care for them, and thus feeling between the two palaces was opened.
嗣秀王 means the succeeding Prince of Xiu; the literal invents 'heir apparent's younger brother' and the false title Xiuxiu.
Only Wuxing has not yet had its commander removed; your servant's heart dares not be at ease."
Only Wuxing has not yet had a commander appointed; your servant's heart dares not be at ease."
Song 除 means appoint; 未除帥 is that no commander has yet been appointed, confirmed by the next unit naming Zhang Zhao to take over Wuxing.
Xiaozong heard and was deeply troubled. Prince Xiuxiu sent the chief minister a note conveying Xiaozong's wish that the ministers return.
Xiaozong heard and was deeply troubled. The Heir Prince of Xiu sent the chief minister a note conveying Xiaozong's wish that the ministers return.
嗣秀王 is the heir/succeeding Prince of Xiu; 'Prince Xiuxiu' again fuses the title into a false personal name.
Xiaozong heard of it and was deeply troubled; Prince of Xiuxiu sent a brief note to the chief minister conveying Xiaozong's wish and ordering the chief ministers to enter again.
Xiaozong heard of it and was deeply troubled; the Heir Prince of Xiu sent a brief note to the chief minister conveying Xiaozong's wish and ordering the chief ministers to enter again.
Same title 嗣秀王; literal 'Prince of Xiuxiu' invents a place-name reading.
Your servant once discussed several matters of the court whose words were not adopted; now Your Majesty has passed Chonghua, Liu Zheng is again chief minister—the realm is greatly fortunate.
Your servant once discussed several matters of the court whose words were not adopted; now Your Majesty has visited Chonghua, Liu Zheng is again chief minister—the realm is greatly fortunate.
過重華 in this court context means paying a visit to Chonghua Palace, not merely passing by it.
Ruyu knew he could not evade responsibility. Precedent required the guard to stand to arms against surprise, yet Palace Commander Guo Gao had no confidant he would trust.
Ruyu knew he could not evade responsibility. Precedent required the guard to stand to arms against surprise, yet there was no one who could speak confidentially to Palace Commander Guo Gao.
殿帥郭杲莫有以腹心語者 means there was no one who could speak to Guo Gao as a confidant; the before reverses that into Guo Gao's own trusting.

Tuozhou brought word back. Ruyu then told Chen Tuan and Yu Duanli, had Guo Gao and infantry commander Yan Zhongye post troops at both palaces, and Li had his kinsman, palace announcer Fu Changchao, secretly make the imperial yellow robe.

Tuozhou brought word back. Ruyu then told Chen Tuan and Yu Duanli, had Guo Gao and infantry commander Yan Zhong post troops at both palaces, and Li had his kinsman, palace announcer Fu Changchao, secretly make the imperial yellow robe.
The personal name is 閻仲 (Yan Zhong); idiomatic Yan Zhongye adds an unsupported syllable.

Tuozhou returned with the reply; Ruyu then told Chen Tuan and Yu Duanli of the affair, had Guo Gao and infantry commander Yan Zhongye guard the Northern and Southern palaces with troops, and Li had his affinal kin, palace announcer Fu Changchao, secretly make the yellow robe.

Tuozhou returned with the reply; Ruyu then told Chen Tuan and Yu Duanli of the affair, had Guo Gao and infantry commander Yan Zhong guard the Northern and Southern palaces with troops, and Li had his affinal kin, palace announcer Fu Changchao, secretly make the yellow robe.
Same Chinese 閻仲; literal Yan Zhongye is the same naming error.

Secretariat drafter Chen Fuliang, censor Wu Lie, and diarist Liu Guangzu were driven out in turn. Sycophants flocked to Tuozhou and hated upright men like mortal foes. The persecution of the scholar-official class had begun.

Secretariat drafter Chen Fuliang, censor Wu Lie, and diarist Liu Guangzu were driven out in turn. Sycophants joined in flattery and hated upright men like mortal foes. The persecution of the scholar-official class had begun.
群憸和附 does not name Tuozhou; 'flocked to Tuozhou' invents an explicit referent absent from this sentence.
Tuozhou drove a wedge between them, sent Zheng to Jiankang, and made Ruyu Grandee for Splendid Happiness and right chief minister.
Tuozhou drove a wedge between them, sent Zheng out as prefect of Jiankang, and appointed Ruyu Grandee for Splendid Happiness and right chief minister.
出正判建康 includes 判, the prefectural posting; 'sent Zheng to Jiankang' omits that office.
Chongxian's first posts were Gentleman for Preserving Righteousness and supervisor of the Raozhou army provision wine depot, then staff officer and military judicial officer of Fuzhou.

Chongxian's first posts were Gentleman for Preserving Righteousness and supervisor of the Raozhou army provision wine depot, then Gentleman for Ceremonial Service and military judicial officer of Fuzhou.
從事郎 is a ranked prestige title, not a functional 'staff officer' post.
Chongxian's first offices were Gentleman for Preserving Righteousness and supervisor of the Raozhou army provision wine depot; he exchanged to staff officer and military judicial officer of Fuzhou.

Chongxian's first offices were Gentleman for Preserving Righteousness and supervisor of the Raozhou army provision wine depot; he exchanged to Gentleman for Ceremonial Service and military judicial officer of Fuzhou.
Same title 從事郎; literal 'staff officer' is the same mistranslation.

He was recalled as director in the Ministry of War, then offered the Department of Seals, declined both, and was made Secretariat rectifier, prefect of Jingjiang, and Guangxi military commissioner and pacification commissioner.

He was recalled as director in the Ministry of War, then offered the Department of Seals, declined both, and was made Auxiliary in the Palace Library, prefect of Jingjiang, and Guangxi military commissioner and pacification commissioner.
直祕閣 is an auxiliary post of the Palace Library, not a Secretariat rectifier.

He was summoned as director in the Ministry of War, soon changed to the Department of Seals, firmly declined both, and was then made rectifier in the Secretariat, prefect of Jingjiang, and Guangxi military commissioner and pacification commissioner.

He was summoned as director in the Ministry of War, soon changed to the Department of Seals, firmly declined both, and was then made Auxiliary in the Palace Library, prefect of Jingjiang, and Guangxi military commissioner and pacification commissioner.
Same office 直祕閣; literal 'rectifier in the Secretariat' is the same institutional error.

Soon Ruyu was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Duke of Yi. Chongxian was promoted to assistant director of the Directorate of Armaments, then the Imperial Treasury, then made secretary. He declined but was not allowed to.

Soon Ruyu was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi. Chongxian was promoted to assistant director of the Directorate of Armaments, then assistant director of the Imperial Treasury, then made secretary. He declined but was not allowed to.
封沂國公 is an enfeoffment, and 改太府監丞 keeps the assistant-director rank; the before collapses both.
